title: [A2 • Band 4.0] Bài 119: The Ginkgo Biloba: The Resilient Living Fossil
passageHtml:
PASSAGE 119 (LEVEL A2 • BAND 4.0)

The Ginkgo Biloba: The Resilient Living Fossil

Paragraph 1. The ginkgo tree is famous for its pretty leaves shaped like small fans. Every autumn, the green leaves turn bright gold. Scientists call the ginkgo a 'living fossil' because this ancient tree lived at the same time as dinosaurs 170 million years ago. Most plants from that time died out long ago, yet the ginkgo tree survived almost unchanged.

Paragraph 2. By the 1600s, scientists in Europe thought the ginkgo tree was completely gone from Earth. However, in 1691, a German doctor named Engelbert Kaempfer visited Japan and saw tall, healthy ginkgo trees there. For hundreds of years, Buddhist monks in China and Japan saved the tree from dying out. The monks planted ginkgo trees near their temples and used the wood for building because it did not burn easily in forest fires.

Paragraph 3. Each ginkgo tree is either male or female. In late autumn, female trees drop soft, yellow seeds onto the ground. When the soft outside part of the seed rots, it makes a terrible smell like old butter or bad meat. Because of this awful smell, city workers never plant female trees along streets. Instead, they only plant male trees.

Paragraph 4. Ginkgo trees are amazingly strong and can live over 1,000 years. They fight off insects, disease, strong storms, and dirty city air. Most amazingly, in August 1945, an atomic bomb exploded over Hiroshima in Japan and burned six old ginkgo trees. Nearby stone buildings fell down, but their deep underground roots stayed alive. Next spring, green leaves grew back on those six trees!

Đoạn 2: "The monks planted ginkgo trees near their temples..."
Đoạn 3: "...terrible smell like old butter or bad meat."

q5.text: Ginkgo leaves turn bright blue in autumn.

steps: Đoạn 1: Lá chuyển màu vàng rực (bright gold), không phải xanh dương.

q6.text: Buddhist monks in Asia helped stop the ginkgo tree from disappearing.

steps: Đoạn 2: Các nhà sư ở Trung Quốc và Nhật Bản đã giữ cho loài cây không bị tuyệt chủng.

q7.text: City workers prefer to plant female ginkgo trees along busy streets.

steps: Đoạn 3: Thành phố tránh trồng cây cái vì mùi hôi, chỉ trồng cây đực.

q8.text: Japanese scientists planted one hundred new ginkgo trees in Hiroshima in 1950.

steps: Đoạn 4: Bài chỉ nói 6 cây sống sót mọc chồi xanh lại vào mùa xuân năm sau, không nhắc năm 1950.
